---
title: "easydta: pairwise DTA meta-analysis (CT vs MRI, paired design)"
output: html_document
---

```{r packages}
if (!requireNamespace("pacman", quietly = TRUE)) {
  install.packages("pacman")
}
pacman::p_load(easydta, ggplot2, grid, gridExtra)
```

```{r load_data}
path <- system.file("extdata/ct_mri.csv", package = "easydta")
d <- utils::read.csv(path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
head(d)
```

```{r reshape}
long <- dta_reshape_pairwise(
  d,
  author       = "author",
  year         = "year",
  intervention = "CT",
  control      = "MRI",
  tp.e = "TP.e", fp.e = "FP.e", fn.e = "FN.e", tn.e = "TN.e",
  tp.c = "TP.c", fp.c = "FP.c", fn.c = "FN.c", tn.c = "TN.c",
  test_var = "test"
)
head(long)
```

```{r fit_pairwise}
pair <- dta_fit_pairwise(long, test_var = "test", nAGQ = 1)
print(pair)
```

```{r compare}
cmp <- dta_compare(pair)
print(cmp)
```

```{r fit_per_arm}
# Fit a single-test bivariate model on each arm so we can draw arm-specific
# forest plots and an overlay SROC.
long_CT  <- subset(long, test == "CT")
long_MRI <- subset(long, test == "MRI")
fit_CT   <- dta_fit_single(long_CT)
fit_MRI  <- dta_fit_single(long_MRI)
```

```{r save_forest_CT}
# Build the wide subset needed by dta_forest() (one row per study, CT arm)
d_CT <- data.frame(
  studlab = paste(d$author, d$year),
  TP = d$TP.e, FP = d$FP.e, FN = d$FN.e, TN = d$TN.e
)
png("forest_CT.png", width = 1400, height = 700, res = 150)
dta_forest(fit_CT, d_CT, studlab = "studlab")
dev.off()
```

```{r save_forest_MRI}
d_MRI <- data.frame(
  studlab = paste(d$author, d$year),
  TP = d$TP.c, FP = d$FP.c, FN = d$FN.c, TN = d$TN.c
)
png("forest_MRI.png", width = 1400, height = 700, res = 150)
dta_forest(fit_MRI, d_MRI, studlab = "studlab")
dev.off()
```

```{r save_sroc_pairwise}
# Per-arm SROC (separate panels, saved side by side as one image)
png("sroc_pairwise.png", width = 1800, height = 900, res = 150)
gridExtra::grid.arrange(
  dta_sroc(fit_CT,  auc_method = "trapz", title = "CT"),
  dta_sroc(fit_MRI, auc_method = "trapz", title = "MRI"),
  ncol = 2
)
dev.off()
```
